purpose: Determine whether materially stronger local MLX model classes can approach the hosted correction shortlist without reopening the rejected small-model prompt matrix.

motivation.completed_local_scope: The completed screen covered Qwen 3.5 0.8B, SmolLM3 3B, and Gemma 4 E2B as 4-bit MLX models. Deterministic repeats and targeted Gemma contract variants reject those exact candidates but do not reject larger local models.
motivation.primary_open_axis: Model capacity is the largest untested local quality axis. Prompt transport and section isolation already received bounded follow-up work, while all completed local repeats were deterministic.

hardware.selection_rule: Run one model at a time and retain sufficient headroom for MLX execution, the prompt, KV cache, and scoring.

stages.scope: The first frozen document, comprising six independently targeted requests, per candidate. Passing results remain part of repeat one.
stages.gate: Load successfully within unified-memory headroom, render the intended chat template, emit a mechanically parseable response, and release memory before the next candidate.

stages.scope: All 60 frozen targets for each technical survivor.
stages.gate: At least 59 mechanically accepted requests, no token cap or gross edit above 30 percent, at least five percent relative aggregate WER reduction, and no more regressions than improvements.
Apply the same quality gates over repeat two independently and both repeats together; record deterministic equality rather than requiring it as a quality claim.

stages.scope: Only the best two-repeat survivor, and only if a pinned 8-bit MLX artifact still fits the 64 GiB execution envelope.
stages.gate: Run the same frozen targets to measure whether 8-bit materially improves semantic regressions or WER. Do not multiply quantizations for candidates already far behind the hosted shortlist.

decision_policy.promotion: A local candidate is product-interesting if it passes both repeats, survives semantic regression review, and offers a useful privacy, latency, or cost tradeoff even if it does not beat the hosted quality ceiling.
decision_policy.rejection: Do not spend further prompt or quantization matrix budget on a candidate that fails the frozen first repeat materially.
decision_policy.runtime_boundary: mlx-lm and the community conversions remain pinned evaluation references over official Apple MLX. Product adoption still requires the repository-owned narrow adapter and model-delivery decision.

claim_limit: This selected synthetic development slice can reject weak local candidates and compare them with identically prompted hosted controls. It cannot establish release quality on human professional podcasts or audiobooks.
